result.summary: The image shows a high-density urban corridor with wide, well-maintained sidewalks and active building frontages. While pedestrian space is generous, the roadway is very wide with at least four travel lanes including a dedicated bus lane, which creates a significant barrier for crossing.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane configuration and overall width of the roadway create a long, unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing with Refuge
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crossing with a pedestrian refuge island to break up the crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at the nearest intersections to shorten crossing distances and increase pedestrian visibility to drivers.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide sidewalk that is currently heavily obstructed by a long construction shed and scaffolding. A buffered area with flex posts provides a degree of separation between the walkway and the multi-lane roadway, though no formal crossings are visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Construction Scaffolding Obstruction
hazards.description: Extensive scaffolding and a construction shed narrow the usable sidewalk width and create a tunnel effect that can limit visibility and personal security.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire building frontage on the left side of the image.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The construction shed structure blocks sight lines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and motorists in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: The vertical supports and roof of the red-topped shed along the curb line.

interventions.title: Enhanced Construction Walkway Lighting
interventions.description: Ensure the interior of the construction shed is brightly lit at all times to maintain visibility and safety for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Hardened Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Replace flexible bollards with more substantial physical protection, such as concrete planters or permanent bollards, to better protect the pedestrian and bike space from vehicle incursions.
